dossier.valuation_method: Probability-weighted EV/EBITDA on normalized EBITDA (composite of 3 branches; weights anchored to the ~10-30% empirical base rate of retail turnarounds: 48% decline / 38% cost-driven stabilization / 14% growth turnaround), cross-checked with a 5-stage DCF (terminal-value sensitivity), specialty-retail peers, and a transaction-triangulated hard-asset floor
dossier.thesis_summary: FLWS is a post-COVID special situation: a multi-brand online gifting franchise whose revenue has declined four straight years (from ~$2.2B FY2022 to ~$1.55B TTM) and whose Adjusted EBITDA fell from $213M to a ~$40M normalized run-rate, with ~$273M cumulative non-cash impairments. A credible, ahead-of-plan cost reset under new management has not stabilized the top line (Q3 FY2026 -11.6%), and lenders suspended the leverage/fixed-charge covenants in May 2025 (a 2027 cliff looms, though the ~$115M 2028 maturity is refinanceable without dilution at $45-55M EBITDA). Disciplining scenario weights to retail-turnaround base rates, FMV is ~$3.55 with a ~$1.55 no-growth floor (asset-supported to ~$2.00 by the owned Medford real estate/orchards and saleable BloomNet). The base-rate-anchored value sits below the consensus turnaround narrative.
key_value_drivers: Where normalized Adjusted EBITDA settles (~$45M decline / ~$67M stabilization / ~$92M turnaround)
Whether revenue plateaus near $1.45B vs. drifting to ~$1.3B (base-rate prior favors continued decline)
Whether the already-achieved $50M cost run-rate sticks net of marketing/MarTech reinvestment (marketing already cut 220-280 bps of sales)
Exit EV/EBITDA multiple (4.5x melting / 5.75x stabilizing / 7x re-rate), all below peer median ~10x
2027 covenant cliff (revert to 2.50x/1.50x) and the financeable ~$115M June-2028 maturity; owned real estate provides sale-leaseback flexibility
key_risks: Structural search/AI traffic erosion makes the revenue decline permanent (modal base-rate outcome)
2027 covenant cliff after the May-2025 covenant holiday; gross leverage ~5x reported Adj EBITDA
Stabilization fails because cost savings are consumed by reinvestment with no demand response
Recurring non-cash impairments signal falling internal forecasts (Consumer Floral at ~zero excess fair value)
Founder dual-class control forecloses takeover-premium optionality
what_would_change_my_mind: Two+ quarters of underlying (ex-deliberate-cut) revenue stabilization with marketing-contribution margin holding
Restored covenant headroom / clean refinancing of the June 2028 maturity, or an announced Medford sale-leaseback
FCF returning toward the $50M+ FY2024 level
Accelerating decline in the Gourmet segment (currently the stable anchor)
A going-concern qualification or a punitive covenant amendment
